title: Sync sprawl: 6 in-repo code paths for the single repo<->active sync relationship; the duplicated pairs have already drifted on a safety fix

evidence.quote: SYNC_DIRS="rules agents skills scripts docs"

# up two levels: .claude/scripts -> .claude -> repo root (this copy is one level deeper than scripts/sync-to-active.sh)
REPO_ROOT="$(dirname "$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")")"
SYNC_SCRIPT="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/sync-to-active.sh"

* PostToolUse hook that auto-syncs ~/.claude changes to continuous-claude repo.
 * Triggers when hooks, skills, rules, scripts, or agents are modified.

observe_how: The 6 paths: (1) scripts/sync-to-active.sh (canonical forward, 271 ln); (2) .claude/scripts/sync-to-active.sh (272-ln near-duplicate; sole diff is the REPO_ROOT depth comment+line — and when forward-synced to ~/.claude/scripts its own dirname(dirname()) math degrades REPO_ROOT to $HOME, making REPO_CLAUDE=$HOME/.claude=ACTIVE_CLAUDE, i.e. a self-copy no-op); (3) scripts/sync-claude.sh (bidirectional, guarded, 140 ln); (4) .claude/scripts/sync-claude.sh (120-ln stale fork — see D7d-02); (5) scripts/post-commit-hook.sh (auto-invokes #1 on every commit); (6) .claude/hooks/src/sync-to-repo.ts (deliberately unregistered after the 2026-06-01 clobber incident but source retained, header still claims 'Registered for: PostToolUse:Write|Edit'). Every sync behavior change must land in 2+ copies; D7d-02 is the proof the double-landing already failed once (guard landed in #3, never in #4). Fix: delete the two .claude/scripts copies (the canonical pair under scripts/ is what docs and the post-commit hook reference) and either delete sync-to-repo.ts or correct its header.
telemetry: git log -1 per copy: scripts/sync-claude.sh @2026-06-01 vs .claude/scripts/sync-claude.sh @2026-05-31 — drift measurable as divergent last-touch dates on supposed duplicates.

title: 11 git-tracked tmpclaude-*-cwd junk artifacts committed into .claude/scripts/ (9) and .claude/hooks/src/ (2), with no .gitignore pattern to stop recurrence

evidence.quote: /c/Users/david.hayes/.claude/scripts

observe_how: git ls-files | grep tmpclaude -> 11 tracked files: .claude/hooks/src/tmpclaude-{681c,9453}-cwd and .claude/scripts/tmpclaude-{0070,0a6c,1fd7,2394,26d6,8ae4,a6eb,afb4,b3ea}-cwd. Each is a ~37-byte single-line cwd capture (Bash-tool working-directory temp files that leaked into source dirs and were swept up by bulk `git add` — e.g. ef00c22 added the scripts batch). Because .claude/scripts and the repo skills/rules dirs forward-sync, the junk also propagates to ~/.claude/ where directory scanners (Codex .agents mirror, skill scanners) enumerate it. grep tmpclaude .gitignore -> no match, so nothing prevents the next batch from being committed. This is a NEW committed-artifact instance of the SEED-06 stray-junk family (SEED-06 itself covers the untracked scripts/.claude/logs artifact). Fix: git rm the 11 files + add `tmpclaude-*` to .gitignore.
telemetry: `git ls-files | grep -c tmpclaude` should be 0 after fix; recurrence detectable by the same count going non-zero.

title: UserPromptSubmit ordering is load-bearing but unenforced and self-contradictorily documented: memory-awareness's bus read (staleness window + busTurn telemetry) depends on bus-session-populator's turn bump landing first, guaranteed only by array position; repo doc claims in-order execution, context-bus header claims 'hook ordering irrelevant', upstream documents parallel execution

evidence.quote: "command": "node C:/Users/david.hayes/.claude/hooks/dist/bus-session-populator.mjs",

* Re-read-on-every-call (design doc section 4.4): readBus re-reads disk EVERY
 * call -- there is no module-level cache. This makes hook ordering irrelevant
 * and survives compaction (the first reader after a compact pays a fresh disk

### Hook Ordering

Hooks execute in the order listed. For PreToolUse, if any hook returns `deny`, subsequent hooks are skipped.

observe_how: What is verified from code: memory-awareness computes focus staleness and logs current_turn from a bus read whose correctness requires bus-session-populator's bumpTurn (bus-session-populator.ts:82-85) to have committed first; the staleness design (isFresh, -1 tolerance) explicitly handles write-AFTER-bump but not read-BEFORE-bump within the same event. The ONLY thing producing that order is array position in settings.json (lines 161 before 166) — no test, lint, comment, or registration guard pins it, and the repo's two written claims contradict each other (README 'execute in the order listed' vs context-bus 'makes hook ordering irrelevant'). Upstream Claude Code documentation states matching hooks for an event run in parallel; if that is the real runtime behavior, the read races the bump: the freshness window nondeterministically widens by one turn (an age-4 item passes as age-3) and the intel-bus current_turn field flickers between N-1 and N for the same turn, corrupting turn-aligned analysis of the B.3b quality-gate telemetry. The D10a-02 pair (memory-awareness emit vs Python braintrust handler) is 'safe' under the same unverified serial assumption. Observe: add a per-hook monotonic timestamp to intel-bus rows from both hooks for 20 prompts and check whether populator's write always precedes memory-awareness's read; then either codify the guarantee in docs/hooks/README.md with a registration-order test, or make memory-awareness self-sufficient (bump-if-unbumped, or read the turn after its own mutateBus round-trip).
telemetry: intel-bus memory_awareness_bus_read rows: current_turn vs the bus file's post-turn value for the same prompt
causal_links: D6a-01 (the serial 13-spawn observation is the empirical counterpoint to upstream's parallel claim — resolving this finding resolves that ambiguity too)

title: Synthetic <task-notification> prompts bump the bus turn counter: turn inflation from background-task noise expires the genuine working set (BUS_STALENESS_MAX_AGE=3), silently disabling recall bias and SESSION FOCUS injection exactly in background-heavy sessions — live consumer blast radius beyond D4a-09's intent stamping

evidence.quote:
* A skipped turn does NOT touch the bus (no turn bump, no intent write) -- the
 * counter only advances on real, recall-worthy prompts, matching what the
 * recall path actually fires on.
export const BUS_STALENESS_MAX_AGE = 3;

observe_how: shouldSeed (lines 58-64) filters only subagent/length/slash — a <task-notification> blob is >15 chars and not a slash command, so it both stamps the intent (D4a-09, S3, no live consumer) AND bumps current_turn, which DOES have a live consumer: extractBusFocus ages every focus term by current_turn - turn_added against the 3-turn window on every memory-awareness fire. Four consecutive background-task notifications (run_in_background completions arrive as UPS prompts; 74 such recall fires in .claude/logs/memory-recall.jsonl) expire the entire working set assembled by bus-tool-populator — the SESSION FOCUS block stops injecting and hybrid-recall query bias drops to zero precisely in the sessions that use background tasks most. The header's stated invariant ('counter only advances on real, recall-worthy prompts') is broken in production: live bus s-mq8noedj-8d40fb04dee1 reached turn 3 with a notification as its current_intent. Fix point is the same synthetic-prompt filter as SEED-13/D2c-01, but it MUST gate the bumpTurn call too, not just intent/recall.
telemetry: 74 rows in .claude/logs/memory-recall.jsonl with intent starting '<task-notification>'; harvest SUMMARY intent-pollution 24.6%
causal_links: instance-of SEED-13; same fix chokepoint as D2c-01
extends D4a-09 (intent stamping, S3/no consumer) with the live-consumer turn-inflation consequence
degrades the B.3b recall-bias win (+15% top-score) that gated the focus-term feature

title: Bus current_intent inherits the recall-intent pollution path: bus-session-populator stamps the raw (sanitized, 120-char) prompt as intent with only length/slash/subagent guards — <task-notification> XML blobs become the session intent (new instance of SEED-13)

observe_how: Payoff: whatever filter lands for SEED-13 (rejecting <task-notification>/system-injected blobs as recall intents) must also be applied in shouldSeed/setIntent here, or the bus's current_intent (surfaced by `/code-intel bus` and any future intent consumer) carries the same pollution.
